annotation.summary_en: Philosophical paper arguing that ethics of social assistive robots in healthcare is too individual-centered and dyadic. Using freedom as non-domination and structural domination, it broadens attention to the political-structural dimension of technology and justice, and lays conceptual groundwork for a more comprehensive ethical approach.
key_provisions_or_claims: Current SAR ethics is individual-centered and limited to dyadic human–robot interaction.
Freedom should be understood also in its political-structural dimension, including non-domination.
Technology has a political dimension shaping sociopolitical structures.
Questions of who decides about SARs and who benefits, given big corporate developers, must be asked.
Ethics of SAR should be reframed in terms of justice across micro, meso and macro levels.
annotation.title_clean: Social Assistive Robotics: An Ethical and Political Inquiry Through the Lens of Freedom
annotation.title_en: Social Assistive Robotics: An Ethical and Political Inquiry Through the Lens of Freedom
